summary: Validates and routes a kb write spec, then hands a record to the raw log. The non-obvious rule lives at the file-note branch: it auto-fills `verified` with the anchor path, which is what makes raw-log stamp the file's live hash and thereby resets the note's freshness. Since 2026-07-30 that auto-fill is conditional on the spec carrying knowledge that implies a read (summary, facets, or body) — a metadata-only edit such as a title or alias fix stamps nothing, because it re-certified notes against bytes nobody looked at. An explicit `verified` in the spec is always honoured; it is the agent's own claim. File-note ids are derived from the path (never supplied), and the two-phase candidate gate runs only for non-file notes.

summary: Validates and routes a kb write spec, then hands a record to the raw log. Two non-obvious rules live in the file-note branch. (1) It auto-fills `verified` with the anchor path, which makes raw-log stamp the file's live hash and reset freshness — conditional since 2026-07-30 on the spec carrying knowledge implying a read (summary, facets, body), so a metadata-only edit stamps nothing; an explicit `verified` is always honoured. (2) Verified 2026-08-03: the same branch OVERWRITES record.anchors with a single entry at spec.path and reads symbols only from spec.anchors[0] — so a file note's extra anchors are unwritable through this path. Secondary anchors exist (raw-log stamps one per `verified` path) but can never be given symbols, and a spec whose anchors[0] is not spec.path has those symbols silently attributed to spec.path instead. File-note ids derive from the path (never supplied); the two-phase candidate gate runs only for non-file notes.
